<entry id="V00616">
<head-word>תָּלַע</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, 
<italic>Hif.</italic> הִתְלִיעַ (denom. of תּוֹלָע) </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to become wormeaten; to decay</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Kil. II, 3 עד שתַּתְלִיעַ until the seed in the ground begins to rot; Y. ib. 27
<sup>d</sup> top עד כמה היא מַתְלַעַת וכ' R. S. to Kil. l. c. (ed. מזרעת, corr. acc.) how long does it take to rot? Three days in moist ground &c. Ḥull. 58
<sup>a</sup> שהִתְלִיעָה, v. אֵב. Y. Ber. II, 5
<sup>c</sup> top והִתְלִיעוּ תאינותיו (not תיה …) and his figs (on the tree) became wormy (or rotten). Cant. R. to IV, 6; Gen. R. s. 47 התליעו they decayed. B. Kam. 52
<sup>a</sup> שה' מתוכו when the board that covered the pit rotted from the inside; a. fr.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to remove the wormy parts from; to sort wood</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Midd. II, 5 ששם … מַתְלִיעִים את העצים for there the priests … sorted the wood for the altar.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>תִּלֵּעַ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to drive vermin off</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Shebi. II, 33
<sup>d</sup> מְתַלְּעִין, v. זָהַם. Y. Sabb. VII, 10
<sup>a</sup> top המעשן המְתַלֵּעַ וכ' he who fumigates plants, or smears them with rancid oil to keep the worms off &c.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. מְתוּלָּע; f. מְתוּלַּעַת; 
<plural-form>pl. מְתוּלָּעִים, מְתוּלָּעִין; מְתוּלָּעוֹת</plural-form>
<italic>wormy</italic>. B. Bath. VI, 2 (93
<sup>b</sup>) תאנים מקבל … מת' וכ' if one buys figs, he must accept ten wormy ones for each hundred; (Y. ed. מַתְלִיעוֹת 
<italic>Hif.</italic>, v. supra).—[</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> (b. h.) 
<italic>to dye scarlet; to clothe in scarlet</italic>.</definition>
<notes>—V. תּוֹלֵעָה.]</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="V00621">
<head-word>תָּלַשׁ</head-word>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to tear, pluck, detach</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Snh. V, 22
<sup>d</sup> top משום תּוֹלֵשׁ, v. קָשַׁשׁ I. Ib. (ref. to Num. XV, 32) מלמד שמצאוהו תולש וכ' the text intimates that they found him tear wood (uproot shrubs) out of the ground; Sabb. 96
<sup>b</sup>; Sifré Num. 113. Bets. 3
<sup>a</sup> גזרה … ויִתְלוֹשׁ we apprehend, lest he may climb up and pluck. B. Kam. VIII, 6 ת' בשערו if one plucks his neighbor’s hair. Y. Sabb. VII, 10
<sup>a</sup> התולש והאורה he who plucks (fruit) or picks (figs); a. fr.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. תָּלוּשׁ; f. תְּלוּשָׁה &c. 
<italic>detached, loose</italic>, opp. מחובר fixed, immovable. Ḥull. 15
<sup>b</sup> ת' ולבסוף חיברו an object originally loose which one afterwards fixed. B. Mets. VII, 2 העושה … ת' מן הקרקע וכ' the journeyman that works … on what is detached from the ground &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pi.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>תִּלֵּשׁ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes> same. Yoma VI, 4 היו מְתַלְּשִׁים בשערו they used to pull the hair of the scapegoat; Tosef. ib. IV (III), 13. Gen. R. s. 34 ומְתַלְּשִׁין ארזי וכ' (not מתליש') they tore cedars of Lebanon out while walking; Yalk. ib. 61.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Nif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>נִתְלַשׁ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be plucked, detached</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mikv. V, 6 גל שנ' if a wave was detached (was thrown on the shore, and its connection with the sea severed); Tosef. ib. IV, 5. Y. Ḥag. I, 76
<sup>c</sup> אם … שנִתְלְשׁוּ וכ' when thou seest Palestinian 
<pgbrk id="pg1674" />townships torn away from their places (their inhabitants driven out), know that they failed to maintain teachers &c.; Lam. R. introd. (R. Abba 2) נִתְלָשׁוֹת; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<entry id="V00626">
<head-word>תְּלַת</head-word>
<head-word>תְּלָתָא</head-word>
<head-word>תְּלָתָה</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> = h. שָׁלשׁ, 
<italic>three</italic>; בת' 
<italic>on the third</italic> (day &c.).</definition>
<notes> Targ. O. Gen. XV, 9 תְּלָתָה ed. Berl. (oth. ed. תִּלְתָּא, read תְּלָתָא); Targ. Y. ib. בר תלת שנין (h. text משלש). Targ. Num. XII, 4. Ib. XXIX, 3; a. v. fr.—Sabb. 87
<sup>a</sup> בת' (sub. בשבא) on the third day of the week. Ib. 36
<sup>a</sup> הני ת' מילי וכ', v. שְׁנֵי. Meg. 6
<sup>b</sup> ת' מאה וכ', v. תָּגָא; a. v. fr.—תלת עסר (תלתא), ת' עשר, ת' עשרה, תְּלֵיסַר, תְּלֵיסְרֵי, תִּלְתֵּיסַר 
<italic>thirteen</italic>. Targ. Num. XXIX, 13, sq. Targ. Gen. XIV, 4; a. fr.—Ber. 4
<sup>a</sup> באורתא דת' וכ', v. נֵגְהָא. Keth. 67
<sup>b</sup> דלא … תליסרי שנין whom he had not seen for thirteen years. Y. Kil. IX, 32
<sup>b</sup> לסוף תלת עשרתי וכ' at the end of thirteen years and thirty days; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּלָתִין</plural-form>
<italic>thirty</italic>. Targ. Gen. V, 3; a. v. fr.—Sabb. 98
<sup>b</sup>. Y. Kil. l. c. כל אינון תַּלְתּוֹיֵי יומיא all these thirty days. Ib. לסוף … ותַלְתָּתוֹי יומייא, v. supra; Y. Keth. XII, 35
<sup>a</sup> bot. תַּלְתִּיתֵי; ib. תְּלֵיתִיתֵי. Y. Shebi. IX, 38
<sup>d</sup> bot. תְּלָתִים שנין thirty years; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00627">
<head-word>תִּלְתָּא</head-word>

<senses>

<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>

<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>having reached one-third of the full growth</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Y. Orl. I, 61
<sup>c</sup> top תִּלְתֵּיהוֹן, v. עַנְקוֹקְלוֹת.—Esp. עגלא ת' 
<italic>a third-grown calf</italic>; oth. [wrong] opin.: 
<italic>in its third year, going on three</italic>; oth. opin. 
<italic>third-born, fat</italic>. [Targ. O. Gen. XV, 9, v. תְּלָתָא.]—Sabb. 136
<sup>a</sup> עיגלא ת' ביממא דשבעה an 
<italic>ʿegla tilta</italic> on its seventh day. Snh. 65
<sup>b</sup>; 67
<sup>b</sup>, v. ברי ch.; Yalk. Ex. 182 תליתא (corr. acc.). Erub. 63
<sup>a</sup> (v. Rashi); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00642">

<hw-number>I</hw-number>

<language-reference>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition />
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>perfect, unblemished</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Tem. 7
<sup>b</sup> (opp. בעל מום); B. Kam. 12
<sup>b</sup>; (Maas. Sh. I, 2 תָּמִים); a. fr.—
<italic>Fem</italic>. תַּמָּה. Sabb. 103
<sup>b</sup>, v. כְּתִיבָה. Succ. 37
<sup>a</sup>, v. לְקִיחָה. Tanḥ. Emor 18 (ref. to ול̇ק̇ח̇ת̇ם̇, Lev. XXIII, 40) בל̇ק̇יח̇ה ת̇מ̇ה וכ' by a real (honest) purchase: thou darest not steal (a Lulab), and stand with it (before God) &c.; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>simple, innocent, artless</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Mekh. Bo, s. 18 ארבעה … ואחד תם וכ' there are four characters in children (as regards their attitude towards religious ceremonies): one is wise, and one is simple &c.; (Yalk. Ex. 225 טיפש); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition> (law) 
<italic>an innocuous animal, one that did injury </italic>
<pgbrk id="pg1675" />
<italic>for the first time</italic>, or 
<italic>before warning had been given</italic>, opp. מוּעָד (v. Ex. XXI, 28-36).</definition>
<notes> B. Kam. I, 4 התם משלם וכ' the 
<italic>tam</italic> pays half-damage from the sale of its own body. Ib. II, 4 איזה הוא תם … משיחזור וכ' when is an animal called 
<italic>tam</italic>?… When it shows its regret for three days, i.e. when it has done an injury and does not repeat it for three days afterwards; ib. (another opin.) ותם כל שיהו וכ' 
<italic>tam</italic> is one which does not gore when children touch it; a. v. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תַּמִּים, תַּמִּין</plural-form>. Ib. I, 4 חמשה ת' וכ' there are five classes of 
<italic>tammin</italic>, i.e. an animal is considered a 
<italic>tam</italic> with regard to five classes of damages (so as to require legal warning): with regard to goring, striking &c.; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00651">
<head-word>תָּמַהּ</head-word>
<head-word>תָּמֵהַּ</head-word>
<language-key>(b. h.;</language-key>
<language-reference>
<xref rid="A00083"> cmp. שָׁמַם)</xref></language-reference>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> [
<italic>to stand still,</italic>] 
<italic>to be astonished, amazed; to wonder; to be undecided</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Pesik. R. addit., s. 1 והבריות תֹּומְהִים לומר וכ' and men wondered, saying, is such a thing possible? Ib. על דור המגדל אתם תֹּומְהִין וכ' you wonder at what occurred to the generation of the tower: has not such a thing occurred &c.? Yalk. Ex. 166 וַיִתְמְהוּ תמיהא גדולה מאד and they wondered exceedingly. Pesik. Haḥod., p. 43
<sup>a</sup> היה … יושב ותָמֵהַּ בלבו וכ' Abraham sat and was undecided in his heart, saying, which shall I choose?; Gen. R. s. 44. Ib. s. 12 מלך … ועמד לו תָּמֵיהַּ a king that rebuked his servant, and he stood there confounded. Ib. תמיה אני איך וכ' I wonder how great men … could disagree on &c. Yeb. 96
<sup>b</sup> תמיה אני אם לא וכ' I should wonder, if this synagogue did not become an idolatrous temple. Arakh. 16
<sup>b</sup> תְּמִיהַנִי יש וכ' I wonder if there is in this generation &c. Pes. VI, 2 אל תִּתְמֵהּ על אלו do not wonder at that Y. ib. 33
<sup>b</sup> bot. תמיהני היאך וכ' I wonder how R. El. could accept such an answer. Yalk. Ex. 202 תְּמַהּ על עצמה היאך וכ' wonder at the very thing, why should leavened matter be forbidden &c.; Pes. 28
<sup>b</sup> תמה על עצמך (corr. acc.); a. fr.</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hif.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הִתְמִיהַּ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition> same. Gen. R. s. 98 same.</definition>
<notes> Gen. R. s. 98 על אלו אתם מַתְמִיהִין you wonder at that? if you were to see היה לכם … להַתְמִיהַּ יותר (not להתמה) you would wonder still more. Pesik. R. s. 28 מַתְמִיהִין (not מתמהין); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to create astonishment, act strangely</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Men. 40
<sup>a</sup> אינו אלא מן המַתְמִיהִין is one of those who make people wonder at their strange conduct; (Ms. M. המוּתְמָהִין 
<italic>Hof</italic>. of those 
<italic>wondered at</italic>).</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—3)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to love miracles, invent miracles</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Yalk. Num. 764 אף אתה מן המַתְמִיהִים art thou, too, of the inventors of miracles?</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Hof.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>הוּתְמַהּ</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition>
<italic>to be wondered at</italic>, v. supra.</definition>
<notes /></sense></senses></binyan></entry>

<sup>a</sup>, v. אֲמֹורָא; a. fr.—Sot. 22
<sup>a</sup> (prov.) תני ת' ולא ידע וכ' a teacher teaches and knows not what he says (repeats verbatim what he has heard without understanding the subject).—

<sup>a</sup> (expl. שיקול הדעת, v. דַּעַת) כגון תרי ת' וכ' when two Tannaim or two Amoraim differ in their opinions, and it has never been decided which is to be adopted in practice. Ib. 63
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. כת' it depends on Tannaim, i.e. Tannaim differ on that point. Ber. 9
<sup>a</sup> והני ת' כהני ת' and those teachers differ on the same principle as these do. Ib. 49
<sup>a</sup> ואת שבקת כל הני ת' ואמוראי וכ' and you ignore all these Tannaim and Amoraim, and act according to Rab’s opinion?; a. v. fr.—V. תַּנַּאי.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<entry id="V00719">
<head-word>תְּנַאי</head-word>
<head-word>תְּנַּיי</head-word>
<pos> m.</pos>
<senses>
<sense>
<definition> (תָּנָה) [
<italic>alternative,</italic>] 
<italic>stipulation, condition, agreement</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Keth. 19
<sup>b</sup> ת' היו דברינו if witnesses say, the transaction to which we have testified was made dependent on a (verbal) condition (and we do not know 
<pgbrk id="pg1680" />that it has been fulfilled). Ib. או דילמא ת' מילתא וכ' or is a statement concerning a condition something different (from a statement concerning a trust, v. אְמָנָה)? Ib. עד אחד אומר ת' … אינו ת' if one of the witnesses says, there was a condition, and the other says, there was none. Kidd. III, 4 כל ת' שאינו … אינו ת' a stipulation of conditions which is not like the stipulations concerning the sons of Gad and Reuben (stating both alternatives, Num. XXXII, 20-23; 29-30) is not valid. Ib. 61
<sup>a</sup>, sq. ת' כפול a double stipulation, an agreement stating both alternatives and their eventual consequences. Gitt. 75
<sup>a</sup> ת' קודם למעשה the condition (in the agreement) preceding the act (e.g. ‘if such and such a thing is done, this shall be thy letter of divorce’, not, ‘this shall be thy letter of divorce, if such and such a thing is done’). Ib. ת' בדבר אחד ומעשה וכ' if the condition concerns one thing, and the consequence another thing (e.g. if you go with your brethren to conquer, you shall have the trans-Jordanic lands); ib.
<sup>b</sup> הכא דת' ומעשה בדבר אחד whereas in this case (‘this shall be thy letter of divorce on condition that thou wilt return to me the paper on which the letter of divorce is written) condition and consequence concern the same thing. Keth. IX, 1 כל המתנה … תְּנָאוֹ בטל if one makes a stipulation which is contrary to what is written in the Torah, his stipulation is void; Y. ib. 32
<sup>d</sup> bot. בת' גוף אבל בת' ממון וכ' this refers only to a condition concerning one’s person (personal rights or duties), but as to a condition concerning money (monetary rights or claims), the agreement (waiving the claim) is valid; Y. Kidd. I, 59
<sup>c</sup> תניי גוף; ib. תְּנָייוֹ. Ib. ת' אפשר … בסופו a condition which he may finally fulfill (depending upon himself). Ex. R. s. 21, v. infra; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תְּנָאִים, תְּנָאִין, תְּנָיִים, תְּנָיִין</plural-form>. Y. B. Bath. V, beg. 15
<sup>a</sup> כתְנָאֵי יהושוע; B. Kam. 80
<sup>b</sup> a. e., v. יְהוֹשׁוּעַ. Gen. R. s. 5 ת' התנה הקב"ה וכ' the Lord (at creation) made stipulations with the sea, that it should be divided before Israel, as it is written (Ex. XIV, 27), ‘and the sea returned … to its former condition (לְאֵיתָנוֹ), לת' שהתנה עמו to the stipulations which &c.; Ex. R. s. 21 לתְנָאוֹ שהתניתי עמו to the condition which I stipulated with it. Y. Sot. VII, beg. 21
<sup>b</sup> כת' שבלבינו לא כת' וכ' (we administer the oath to thee) according to the conditions in our mind, not according to the conditions (mental reservations) in thy mind. Ib. שלא יאמרו יש ת' לשבועות that people should not say, mental reservations in oaths are permissible. Y. Kidd. I, 58
<sup>c</sup> בתניים שבו קידש he betrothed her by the stipulations in the document (although the material on which it was written was forbidden for use), opp. בגופו with the object itself; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<senses>
<sense>
<definition>, </definition>
<notes /></sense>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to repeat, do a second time</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. II Sam. XX, 10. Targ. I Sam. XXVI, 8 (ed. Wil. אֶשְׁנֵי). Targ. I Kings XVIII, 34. Targ. Job XXIX, 22 (ed. Wil. 
<italic>Pa.</italic>). Targ. Prov. XXVI, 11 דתָאנֵי ed. Lag. (ed. Wil. דתָנֵי); a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to tell, relate; to teach</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Ps. L, 6. Ib. XLIX, 14 (Ms. 
<italic>Pa.</italic>). Ib. CXLVII, 19. Targ. Y. Deut. V, 5 למִתְנְיָא (ed. Vien. למִתַּנְיָא 
<italic>Ithpe.</italic>); a. fr.—Esp. (denom. of מתניתא) 
<italic>to teach</italic> or 
<italic>study Mishnah</italic> or 
<italic>Boraitha</italic>; in gen. 
<italic>to report a tradition, teach, study</italic>. Erub. 36
<sup>b</sup> ליתא למתניתן מדתָנֵי איו דת' איו וכ' our Mishnah is no authority, as it is contradicted by what Ayo teaches, for Ayo taught &c. Yoma 27
<sup>b</sup> והא אנן לא תְּנָן הכי but we have not so learned in the Mishnah! Ib. הך … קתני הך … לא קתני the Mishnah speaks of that which, if neglected, can be remedied; that which cannot be remedied it does not mention. Sabb. 2
<sup>a</sup> תנן התם וכ' there (in the Mishnah, Shebu. I, 1) we read &c. Ib.
<sup>b</sup> מאי שנא הכא דת' … ומ"ש התם דת' וכ' why does the Mishnah here read …, and there &c.? Ber. 8
<sup>b</sup> תְּנִינָא וכ' we are taught in the Mishnah &c. Ib. 2
<sup>a</sup> דקת' מאימתי, v. קָאֵי. Ib. כדתַנְיָא as it is stated (in the Boraitha). Yoma 26
<sup>a</sup> לכדתניא (the word 
<italic>peder</italic> is needed) to intimate the law taught in the Boraitha. Ib. והתניא וכ' but has it not been taught &c.?; ib. 28
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr.—Ber. 28
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. והתניא and so it has been taught.—Y. Ḥall. II, 58
<sup>c</sup> ר' יונה ת' דר"ש וכ' R. Jonah taught (and adopted) the opinion of R. S. b. J.—Y. Kidd. I, 58
<sup>c</sup> bot. תמן תנינן there (in a Mishnah) we read &c. Meg. 24
<sup>b</sup> לימא תנינן להא דתָנוּ רבנן וכ' shall we say that we are here taught that which the Rabbis have taught &c. (i.e. is this a confirmation of what &c.)?—Ber. 13
<sup>a</sup>, a. fr. תָּנוּ רבנן (abbrev. ת"ר) the Rabbis have taught (introducing a discussion); a. v. fr.—[In Talm. Babli תנן refers to Mishnah, תניא to Boraitha.]</notes></sense></senses>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Pa.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>תַּנֵּי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to change</italic>.</definition>
<notes>. Targ. Job XIV, 20.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to tell, relate; to teach</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Gen. XXII, 20. Ib. XXXII, 6. Targ. Ps. XXX, 10 הַיְתַנּוּן ed. Lag. (Ms. אפשר דיתנון; ed. Wil. החויתון; oth. ed. החויתינון, corr. acc.). Targ. II Chr. IX, 2; a. fr.—Ber. 49
<sup>a</sup> ברכת … וחַנּוּיֵי קא מְתַנִּינָא Ms. M. (or מַתְנִינָא 
<italic>Af.</italic>; ed. מְתַנִּינָן or מַתְנִינָן) I have not learned the benediction over food, and shall I teach (Mishnah)?</notes></sense></senses></binyan>
<binyan>
<binyan-name>Af.</binyan-name>
<binyan-form>אַתְנֵי</binyan-form>
<senses>
<sense>
<number>1)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to stipulate, agree, make a condition</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Targ. Y. Ex. IV, 24.—Keth. 3
<sup>a</sup> כיון דאיבעי ליה לאַתְנוּיֵי ולא א' וכ' because he ought to have made it a condition (not to count so common an obstacle as the absence of a ferry), and he did not make it, he has to take the consequences. Shebu. 11
<sup>b</sup> וכי קיימי ב"ד ומַתְנוּ משום עורה Ms. M. (ed. וקיימי ב"ד ומתנו אדעתא דעורה) did the court establish a general law (that dead sacrificial animals need not be redeemed,) and stipulate that it must be redeemed for the value of its skin?; a. e.</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>—2)</number>
<definition>
<italic>to relate, teach</italic>.</definition>
<notes> Ber. 8
<sup>b</sup> איכא דמַתְנֵי להא וכ' some one quoted that opinion of R. A. bar Ḥ. with reference to what has been taught, ‘R. S. b. Y. says &c.’ Keth. 17
<sup>a</sup> sq. וה"מ למאן דקרי ותני אבל למאן דמתני וכ' this has been said concerning the funeral only of one who was versed in Bible and a student of 
<pgbrk id="pg1682" />Mishnah, but as regards one who was a teacher of Mishnah, there is no limit (of attendance at his funeral). Ḥull. 48
<sup>a</sup> הא … אתון אהא מַתְנִיתוּן לה אנן אדרבא מַתְנִינָן לה you report that action of R. N. … in connection with this, we report it in connection with what Raba said &c.; a. fr.</notes></sense></senses></binyan>

<italic>Fem</italic>. תִּנְיָינֵיתָא, תִּנְיָנֵ', תִּנְיֵיתָא, תִּנְיִתָא, תִּי'. Targ. Zech. VI, 2. Targ. Job XL, 5. Targ. Is. XLIII, 2. Targ. O. Gen. IV, 19 (ed. Vien. תִּנְיָתָא; Y. תִּנְיָנְתָא); a. fr.—Lev. R. s. 9 שבתא קמייתא ת' וכ' the first, the second, and the third Sabbath. Y. Maas. Sh. IV, end, 55

<number>1)</number>

<notes> Kil. I, 4 הת' והחזרד וכ' the apple and the crab-apple …, although resembling each other, are heterogeneous (כִּלְאַיִם). Cant. R. to VIII, 5 מה ת' זה עושה וכ' as the apple tree brings forth fruit in Sivan, so the Law was given in Sivan. Ib. כל אילן … ות' זה מוציא וכ' every other tree produces first its leaves, and then its fruit (buds), but the apple tree produces its buds first, and then its leaves; even so Israel advanced doing to hearing; Sabb. 88
<sup>a</sup>; Cant. R. to II, 3. Ib. מה ת' זה אתה נותן בו איסר וכ' (not איסור) as the apple, for which you pay an Isar and whose scent you enjoy many times, so &c. Num. R. s. 19
<sup>16</sup> (expl. הר ההר, Num. XX, 2</notes></sense>
<sense>
<number>2)</number>
<definition> הר על גבי הר כת' קטן על גבי ת' גדול a hill upon a hill, like a small apple on a large apple; a. fr.—
<plural-form>Pl. תַּפּוּחִים, תַּפּוּחִין</plural-form>.</definition>
<notes> Cant. R. to II, 5 אלו ההגדות … כת' that means the Hăgadoth whose flavor and taste are like those of apples. Men. 28
<sup>b</sup> תַּפּוּחֵי הכרתיים, v. כְּרֵתִי; a. fr.—2) (from its shape) 
<italic>a</italic>) ת' עקב 
<italic>the fleshy part of the heel</italic>. Pesik. Par., p. 36
<sup>b</sup> ת' עקיבו וכ' the apple of Adam’s heel outshone the globe of the sun; ib. Aḥăré, p. 170
<sup>a</sup>; Lev. R. s. 20; a. e.—b) 
<italic>pile</italic>, esp. 
<italic>the place on the altar where the ashes were piled up</italic>. Ab. Zar. IV, 8 אע"פ … ונותן לת' although the gentile may take grapes in his hand and put them on the pile. Tam. II, 2 החלו … ע"ג ת' והת' היה וכ' they began to put the ashes on the 
<italic>tappuaḥ</italic>, and the 
<italic>t.</italic> was in the centre of the altar, containing at times as much as &c.; Ḥull. 90
<sup>b</sup>. Ib. חולצו לת' he takes it (the nervus ischiadicus) out, and throws it on the 
<italic>tappuaḥ</italic>; a. e.</notes></sense></senses></entry>

<sup>a</sup> הוציא … ותָפְחָה וכ' if he carried out (on the Sabbath) the size of half a dried fig, intending to sow it, and it swelled (to the size of a whole fig) &c., v. צָמַק. Tosef. Shebi. II, 14 כדי שיִתְפַּח in order that it (the dung) may swell (or 
<italic>become moist</italic>, v. תָּפַח III). Mikv. VII, 7 כדי שיִתְפְּחוּ המים that the water may rise in volume. Num. R. s. 9
<sup>21</sup> ויִתְפַּח צוארה (not ותפח) and her throat shall swell. Y. Ter. II, 41
<sup>d</sup> top אתה רואה את הצמק כאילו ת' look upon the shrivelled fruit as if it were blown up (of full size). Ib. לִתְפּוֹחַ, v. תֶּפַח; a. fr.—
<italic>Part. pass</italic>. תָּפוּחַ 
<italic>round and smooth</italic>. Y. Nidd. III, 50
<sup>d</sup> bot. ראשו ת' כתורמוס the head (of the embryo) is round and smooth as a lupine; כקרקבן as a bird’s maw.</notes></sense></senses></entry>
